methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series B → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.9x) to $1.0B total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Transportation (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 3 same-sector peers exist in Transportation, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
JetZero is a Series B transportation company founded by Tom O'Leary and Mark Page that has raised $1.0B+ to date. The broader transportation sector comp universe includes 7 private peers (Rivian, The Boring Company, Einride, Arc Boats, Parallel Systems among them) and no public comparables; however, same-stage and adjacent-stage peers within transportation proved insufficient (fewer than 3 datapoints in each filtered cohort) to support peer-median triangulation.

The stage-progression method is the primary applicable approach given data constraints. Using total capital raised of $1.0B as a proxy for current valuation, a typical Series B-to-next-stage step-up multiplier of 1.9x yields an implied valuation of $1.9B. This single-method triangulation produces a range of $1.6B (low) to $2.2B (high), centered at $1.9B median.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $1.6B to $2.2B, with $1.9B as the central estimate. Material uncertainties include the lack of narrow-universe peer comparables to validate the step-up multiple and absence of recent private fundraising data from same-stage transportation companies to calibrate the progression assumption. The reliance on a single method reflects limited market data rather than analytical confidence; investor conviction should weight management track record, capital efficiency, and pathway to revenue alongside this structural valuation.
